elements.element: Customer is not obligated to obtain hosted analytics services exclusively from Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 designates Vendor as a “non-exclusive provider,” and Section 12.3 expressly states that Customer may engage any supplier and has made no exclusivity commitment.

elements.element: Vendor is not designated as Customer's sole supplier or provider.
elements.evidence: The rendered Section 2.2 removes “sole and exclusive” and replaces it with “non-exclusive.”

elements.element: Any exclusivity obligation binding Customer is limited to a defined product category.

elements.element: Any exclusivity obligation binding Customer lasts no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity obligation binds Customer, so the condition requiring a 12-month limit is demonstrably absent. The reference to the term in Section 2.2 applies only to Vendor's non-exclusive status.

elements.element: Any exclusivity obligation binding Customer ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet applicable service levels.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity obligation binds Customer, so the condition requiring this automatic termination trigger is demonstrably absent.

result.reason: The operative redline minimally replaces the sole-and-exclusive appointment with a non-exclusive appointment. Read with Sections 2.1 and 12.3, it imposes no exclusivity, sole-supplier, minimum-purchase, or future-order obligation on Customer. The preferred position is fully met; the fallback is also met because no exclusivity obligation exists to require category, duration, or termination limitations.
